reason: A check-then-open done in two transactions let parallel callers each open a base. The lesson is class-level: any check that gates a create needs one cross-process lock held across both, plus a reproduction that shows the race before the fix.

Episode fixed a store upgrade that raced across processes. The SQLite backup-in-transaction and WAL facts were found by probe and are not in this skill; they are the durable part of the lesson for any check-then-swap under a lock.

The spawn race needed a marker written under the lock, because the child's row appears only after it starts. Parent-pid checks fail once the parent server restarts. This is the same check-then-create class and the skill should carry it.
